lessons.title: Define a workflow
lessons.subtitle: Week 12: Third milestone: build a workflow
lessons.body:
A workflow is a sequence of steps with inputs, outputs, and responsibilities. AI can support a step without replacing the entire process.

Offline practice: Map collect notes → draft summary → check claims → revise → save. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A workflow is a sequence of steps with inputs, outputs, and responsibilities. AI can support a step without replacing the entire process.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
lessons.sourceName: Google Machine Learning Crash Course — further reading

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains “Define a workflow”?
options: A workflow is a sequence of steps with inputs, outputs, and responsibilities. AI can support a step without replacing the entire process.
A polished AI answer is enough evidence that every claim is correct.
The human learner never needs to check the result.
Every task requires training a new model.
questions.explanation: A workflow is a sequence of steps with inputs, outputs, and responsibilities. AI can support a step without replacing the entire process.

questions.prompt: For the activity “Map collect notes → draft summary → check claims → revise → save.”, which approach demonstrates learning?
options: Complete the activity, explain your reasoning, and record a limitation.
Share someone else’s private information to make the example realistic.
Treat an unverified generated response as final evidence.
Skip the activity and copy an unrelated answer.
questions.explanation: The activity asks you to apply this lesson. A written explanation and limitation make your understanding reviewable; a copied result alone does not.

questions.prompt: You return to the “Define a workflow” lesson after a break without internet. What can you do next?
options: Recall the key idea, check saved notes, and complete the offline activity.
Assume a cloud assistant will respond without a connection.
Wait until you can buy a paid AI subscription.
Delete your previous work and start the whole course again.
questions.explanation: The lesson and practice do not require an online tool. Retrieval and a small saved activity help you resume.

lessons.title: Human review gates

lessons.title: Repeatable evaluation
lessons.subtitle: Week 12: Third milestone: build a workflow
lessons.body:

lessons.title: Offline fallback
lessons.subtitle: Week 12: Third milestone: build a workflow
lessons.body:
A workflow should remain useful when connectivity fails. Save essential references and provide manual steps for the parts that normally require a service.

Offline practice: Write an offline version of your summary workflow with no online assistant. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: A workflow should remain useful when connectivity fails. Save essential references and provide manual steps for the parts that normally require a service.

lessons.title: Month-three demonstration
lessons.subtitle: Week 12: Third milestone: build a workflow
lessons.body:
A demonstrated workflow includes steps, review criteria, sample outputs, a fallback, and observed limitations. Show failures and corrections as well as successes.

Offline practice: Demonstrate your workflow using fictional inputs and record one change prompted by a failed check. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A demonstrated workflow includes steps, review criteria, sample outputs, a fallback, and observed limitations. Show failures and corrections as well as successes.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
